content.title: TINY {{HABITS}} THAT PAY OFF WAY MORE THAN YOU'D EXPECT
facts: **Chew each bite 20 times** — this slows digestion way down, easing bloating and helping you naturally eat less without even trying.
**Stand up every 45 minutes** — even a 2-minute break from sitting keeps blood sugar from spiking and wakes up sluggish leg muscles.
**Breathe through your nose during exercise** — it filters and warms the air, keeping your airways calmer and your stamina steadier.
**Rub your ears for 30 seconds each morning** — this stimulates pressure points linked to alertness and can gently perk up circulation.
**Eat your protein first at meals** — going protein-first blunts the blood sugar spike that comes from carbs eaten alone.
**Unclench your jaw every time you check your phone** — most people carry hidden tension there, and releasing it eases tension headaches.
**Wiggle your toes before getting out of bed** — this wakes up circulation in your feet and can ease that stiff, cold-foot feeling in the morning.
**Let your eyes drift to something 20 feet away every 20 minutes** — this relaxes the eye muscles and cuts down on screen-related strain.
**Follow along** – for more small daily habits that quietly add up to a healthier you.
content.caption:
A few of these are worth slowing down on. Take chewing — chewing each bite 20 times isn't just about manners, it gives your stomach time to signal 'full' to your brain before you overeat, and it breaks food down enough that nutrients actually get absorbed properly. Then there's the jaw unclenching habit — most of us clamp down without noticing, especially while scrolling, and that constant low-grade tension is a sneaky trigger for tension headaches and jaw pain by the end of the day. And eating protein first at meals genuinely changes your blood sugar curve — it slows how fast sugar from the rest of your meal hits your bloodstream, which means less of that crash-and-crave cycle an hour later. Everyone's body is different, so notice what actually feels different for you.
